newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to let more Palestinians in for work.
newsitem.headline: Israel to let more Palestinians in for work.

text.p: Israel said on Tuesday it would permit more Palestinians to cross into the Jewish state for work, further easing a closure imposed on the West Bank and Gaza last month after an Islamist bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe.

"Tomorrow there will be a significant easing of the closure and we will reach a situation where all aspects of (Palestinian) life will become fairly reasonable," said Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.

The army said it would allow 55,000 Palestinians from the West Bank and Gaza to enter Israel but Palestinians have said similar Israeli measures have resulted in far fewer Palestinians actually reaching their jobs.

"Palestinian over the age of 30 who are married will be permitted to enter Israel starting tomorrow," an army spokesman said. Israel believes the marriage requirement and age limit cut the risk of suicide bombers entering its territory.

A Palestinian bomber killed three Israeli women at a Tel Aviv cafe on March 21, three days after Israel launched the construction on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem which Palestinians view as the capital of their future state.
The settlement building touched off a wave of West Bank clashes in which Israeli troops killed seven Palestinians.

"Even when Israel announces the easing of the closure it takes measures to prevent many people from reaching their jobs in Israel," said Hassan Abu Libdeh, head of the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics (PCBS), after a similar Israeli announcement earlier this month.
Palestinians view the periodic closures as a form of collective punishment.
